목요일.x: I have a test on Thursday.
목요일.e: 'Wood day' — named for Jupiter, the wood planet.

죽다.x: The flowers died because I didn't water them.
죽다.e: 죽 also means rice porridge — a different word.
죽다.t: For elders and respected people use 돌아가시다. Casual slang: 배고파 죽겠어요 'I'm starving.'

용돈.x: I get an allowance from my parents every month.
용돈.e: 용 'use' plus native 돈 'money': money for personal use.
용돈.t: Adult children also give 용돈 to parents: 부모님께 용돈을 드리다. Pronounced [용똔].

주차장.x: There's a big parking garage under the department store.
주차장.e: -장 = place for an activity: 주차장, 운동장, 시장.

노란색.x: In fall, ginkgo leaves turn yellow.
노란색.e: From native 노랗다 'to be yellow', modifier 노란, plus 색.

국어.m: Korean (as a school subject); national language
국어.ex: 저는 학교에서 국어 시간을 제일 좋아했어요.
국어.x: I liked Korean class the most in school.
국어.t: Koreans call their own school subject 국어; foreigners learn 한국어.

격려하다.x: The coach encouraged the players in a loud voice.
격려하다.t: Pronounced [경녀하다] — nasalization changes both ㄱ and ㄹ.

상대 팀.x: We beat the other team 3 to 1.

협조.ex: 이번 행사에 여러분의 많은 협조를 부탁드립니다.
협조.x: We ask for your full cooperation with this event.
협조.t: Common in notices: 협조 부탁드립니다 'we ask for your cooperation'.

구조 조정.ex: 회사가 구조 조정을 해서 직원 백 명이 회사를 떠났어요.
구조 조정.x: The company restructured, so a hundred employees left.
구조 조정.e: Literally 'adjusting the structure'; often a polite word for cutting jobs.

방안.m: plan, measure, way (to solve a problem)
방안.ex: 정부가 교통 문제를 해결할 방안을 찾고 있어요.
방안.x: The government is looking for a way to solve traffic problems.
방안.e: Literally 'method plan': a concrete way to deal with something.
방안.t: Typical collocations: 방안을 마련하다 'to work out a plan', 방안을 찾다 'to look for a way'.

평론가.ex: 영화 평론가들이 그 감독의 새 영화를 칭찬했어요.
평론가.x: Film critics praised the director's new movie.

빙하.x: Glaciers are melting because of global warming.

석탄.x: In the old days, people heated their homes with coal.

정교하다.x: This watch was made very intricately.

공표.ex: 선거 직전에는 여론 조사 결과를 공표할 수 없습니다.
공표.x: Poll results cannot be made public right before an election.

항체.x: When you get a vaccine, your body produces antibodies.
항체.e: Literally 'resisting body', a direct match for 'anti-body'. 항- = anti-: 항생제, 항암.

능가하다.m: to surpass, to exceed, to outdo
능가하다.ex: 올해 매출은 작년 수준을 크게 능가했습니다.
능가하다.x: This year's sales far exceeded last year's level.

창안하다.m: to originate, to create (a new idea or method), to invent
창안하다.ex: 그는 새로운 교육 방법을 창안해서 유명해졌어요.
창안하다.x: He became famous for creating a new teaching method.
창안하다.e: Literally 'create a plan' — coming up with something brand-new.
창안하다.t: 고안 = devising a practical device or solution; 창안 = originating a new idea, theory, or method.

호의적.ex: 새 영화에 대한 관객들의 반응이 대체로 호의적이었어요.
호의적.x: Audience reaction to the new movie was mostly favorable.

천편일률적.x: Dramas these days are all so cookie-cutter.
천편일률적.e: Literally 'a thousand poems, one rhythm' — everything sounds the same.

한결같이.ex: 그는 십 년 동안 한결같이 아내를 사랑했어요.
한결같이.x: He loved his wife unchangingly for ten years.
한결같이.e: From 한결 'one grain, one texture' plus 같이 'like' — always the same.
한결같이.t: Pronounced [한결가치] — ㅌ before 이 becomes ㅊ (palatalization).

학수고대.m: eagerly waiting, looking forward to impatiently
학수고대.ex: 아이들은 여름 방학을 손꼽아 학수고대하고 있어요.
학수고대.x: The kids are counting the days, eagerly waiting for summer vacation.
학수고대.e: Literally 'waiting painfully with a neck stretched out like a crane'.
학수고대.t: Pronounced [학쑤고대]; usually as the verb 학수고대하다.

공로.ex: 선생님은 교육 발전에 대한 공로로 상을 받으셨어요.
공로.x: The teacher received an award for contributions to education.
공로.e: Literally 'merit and toil' — credit earned by hard work.
공로.t: Pronounced [공노] — nasalization of ㄹ after ㅇ.

불구속.m: without detention, without arrest (while under investigation or trial)
불구속.ex: 경찰은 그를 불구속 상태로 조사하고 있습니다.
불구속.x: Police are investigating him without detaining him.
불구속.e: Literally 'not bound' — the suspect stays free during the process.
불구속.t: Very common in news as 불구속 기소 'indicted without detention'.

전염성.ex: 이 병은 전염성이 강해서 조심해야 합니다.
전염성.x: This disease is highly contagious, so you need to be careful.
전염성.e: Literally 'nature of passing on an infection'. -성 = quality or nature: 가능성, 중요성.
전염성.t: Pronounced [저념썽]; usually paired with 강하다 or 높다: 전염성이 강하다.

항의하다.x: The customer complained to the manager about the bad service.
항의하다.t: Use 에게/에 for the target: 회사에 항의하다; 시위 is a street protest, 항의 is any complaint.

입만 살다.m: to be all talk (and no action) (lit. only the mouth is alive)
입만 살다.ex: 그 사람은 입만 살아서 실제로 하는 일은 없어요.
입만 살다.x: He's all talk and never actually does anything.
입만 살다.e: Only the mouth is 'alive' and working, while the hands and feet do nothing.
입만 살다.t: Critical and casual. Pronounced [임만 살다]. Usually in the past form: 입만 살았네! 'All talk!'

사촌이 땅을 사면 배가 아프다.forms: 사촌이 땅을 사면 배가 아프다더니 · 사촌이 땅을 사면 배가 아프다고
사촌이 땅을 사면 배가 아프다.m: to be jealous of others' good fortune (lit. if your cousin buys land, your stomach hurts)
사촌이 땅을 사면 배가 아프다.ex: 사촌이 땅을 사면 배가 아프다더니, 친구가 승진하니까 괜히 샘이 나요.
사촌이 땅을 사면 배가 아프다.x: It's true what they say about envy: my friend got promoted, and I can't help feeling jealous.
사촌이 땅을 사면 배가 아프다.e: Even when your own cousin (사촌, a relative four degrees removed) buys land, your stomach aches with envy.
사촌이 땅을 사면 배가 아프다.t: Pronounced [사초니 땅을 사면 배가 아프다]. 배가 아프다 alone is a common casual way to say 'to be jealous', e.g. 배 아파요.

계엄령.x: When martial law was declared, soldiers were deployed in the streets.
계엄령.t: Pronounced [계엄녕] — ㄹ after ㅁ becomes ㄴ.

종파.ex: 불교에도 여러 종파가 있어서 수행 방법이 조금씩 달라요.
종파.x: Buddhism also has several sects, so their practices differ slightly.
종파.t: 종파 is common for Buddhism and Islam, while 교파 is the usual word for Christian denominations.

척수.ex: 그는 사고로 척수를 다쳐 걷지 못하게 되었습니다.
척수.x: He injured his spinal cord in an accident and became unable to walk.
척수.t: Pronounced [척쑤]; don't confuse 척수 (spinal cord) with 척추 (the spine bones themselves).

용질.x: In sugar water, sugar is the solute and water is the solvent.

액자소설.ex: 액자소설은 이야기 속에 또 다른 이야기가 들어 있는 형식이에요.
액자소설.x: A frame story is a form with another story inside the story.
액자소설.e: Literally 'picture-frame novel' — an outer story framing an inner one.

경질하다.m: to replace, to dismiss and replace (an official)
경질하다.ex: 대통령은 사고의 책임을 물어 장관을 경질했습니다.
경질하다.x: The president replaced the minister, holding him responsible for the accident.
경질하다.e: Literally 'change and alternate': swapping out a person in office.
경질하다.t: A news word for firing high officials, coaches or executives; 경질되다 is the passive.

퍽이나.ex: 다들 우는 걸 보니 시험이 퍽이나 어려웠나 봐요.
퍽이나.x: Seeing everyone cry, the exam must have been really hard.
퍽이나.t: In casual speech it's often sarcastic: 퍽이나 잘도 하겠다 'Yeah, as if you'd do it.'
